title: Cap. VI Arg. 3: Hague reply — foresight faith not cause; Davenant — word-catching and merit
pass_a_gloss: But the Hague Colloquy respondents reply; First, that they never set down foresighted faith as the cause of election, and therefore do not contravene the Scriptures, which establish God's εὐδοκία, or good pleasure alone, as its cause. Indeed in so many words they profess that the cause why God elected any particular person to salvation is not that person's faith, but only good pleasure, grace, yea the mere grace of God. But all these things are mere word-catching. For those who set down the act of persevering faith as a condition required by God, at the intuition of which he always elects, and for whose absence he always passes by, ascribe to faith a causal force, yea a meritorious one, in that sense in which the word merit is used by Augustine and the rest of the theologians in disputes against the Pelagians. So Augustine, Who would say that he who has already begun to believe merits nothing from him in whom he has believed?
pass_b_english: The Hague Colloquy speakers answer first: they never call foresighted faith the cause of election, so they do not fight Scripture naming εὐδοκία — good pleasure alone — as cause. They even say outright that why God elects any one person to salvation is not that person's faith, but only good pleasure, grace, mere grace. Word-catching, all of it. Whoever makes persevering faith the condition God requires — at whose sight he always elects, and for whose absence he always passes by — gives faith causal force, even meritorious force, in Augustine's anti-Pelagian sense of merit. So Augustine: who would say that one who has already begun to believe merits nothing from him in whom he believed?
source_text: Sed respondentes Colloquutores Hagienses; Primo, se nunquam ponere praevisam fidem esse causam electionis, ac proinde non contravenire Scripturis, quae statuunt Dei εὐδοκίαν, vel solum beneplacitum esse ejus causam. Imo totidem verbis profitentur, causam, cur Deus singularem aliquam personam elegerit ad salutem, non esse fidem ejus, sed solum beneplacitum, gratiam, imo meram gratiam Dei. Sed haec omnia sunt mera verborum aucupia. Nam qui ponunt actum fidei perseverantis esse conditionem a Deo requisitam, ad cujus intuitum semper eligit, et ob cujus absentiam semper praeterit, ii vim causalem fidei adscribunt, imo meritoriam, eo sensu quo meriti vocabulum ab Augustino reliquisque Theologis in disceptationibus contra Pelagianos usurpatur. Sic Augustinus, Quis dicat illum qui jam coepit credere, ab illo in quem credidit nihil mereri?
